concerns.text: T013a (conformer gen) and T014a (variance calc) are listed as independent or parallel, but T014a explicitly requires the 3D conformer ensembles generated by T013a. Furthermore, T015 (correlation) and T019a (regression) consume the output of T014a. The current ordering implies T014a can run before T013a completes, violating the producer-consumer dependency. T014a must strictly follow T013a.

T013b (success rate), T013c (sampling), and T013d (error handling) are all listed as depending on T013a, but T013c (sampling) logically requires the success rate from T013b to determine if the dataset size is sufficient before sampling. T013c should depend on T013b, not just T013a. Similarly, T013d (logging failures) is a reporting step that should occur after the generation loop (T013a) but before downstream consumption; its placement as a parallel sibling to T013b/c is ambiguous and risks race conditions if T013b/c rely on the final failure count.

Phase 6 (Scaling Analysis) tasks T026-T030 are marked as [P] (parallel) or loosely dependent, but T027 (power-law regression) and T029 (visualization) strictly require the output of T026 (complexity metrics) and T028 (topology metrics). T027 cannot run before T026. T030 (report update) requires T029. The current grouping suggests these can run in parallel, which is semantically impossible as they form a linear data-flow chain.

T020 (scaffold-based cross-validation) is listed as depending on Foundational and US2, but it consumes the model predictors defined in T019a. T019a (model implementation) must complete before T020 (validation) can execute. The current dependency list for T020 is too broad and misses the direct dependency on T019a, risking a consumer-before-producer violation if T020 is scheduled before T019a.

T014b (outlier flagging) and T014c (output formatting) are marked [P] (parallel). However, T014c (formatting) requires the 'is_outlier' column generated by T014b. T014c cannot run in parallel with T014b; it must strictly follow it. The [P] tag is incorrect here.
